description:
Goal
Every compiler2/fz2 production emitter passes existing raw semantic authorities and direct raw scalars. Handlers alone inspect, transform, or retain callback-scoped values. With no matching handler, telemetry performs no payload construction, traversal, transformation, or allocation, and NullTelemetry can erase the call path.

Proven model failures
The original guard trusted helper parameters without proving caller provenance, admitted computed locals when assignment, branch, or return use looked semantic, hand-listed sink APIs, missed UFCS and indirect function-item uses, and resolved helpers by names too loosely. TypeName and JobEffects were cloned or reconstructed at telemetry seams. Activation-input events repeated one completion per key. Runtime dbg output was semantic program output mis-modeled as telemetry: the original FFI callback was an indirect emitter helper, while deferring emission required a telemetry-only Vec copy.

Resolution
The guard now inventories payload-bearing Telemetry, TelemetryExt, Span, DetachedSpan, and ExecutionContext APIs; rejects eager payload calls; recognizes method and UFCS forms; and bans sink APIs or emitter helpers used as function items, fields, returns, or aliases. Its callable graph uses scan module, impl owner, name, and arity; owned scalar parameters recursively validate every direct callsite; borrowed scalar parameters validate caller provenance like owned scalars, while borrowed domain parameters recursively require existing places or references at every known callsite; recursion, unknown callsites, computed locals, and semantic-use laundering fail. Qualified unresolved free-helper calls conservatively join known helper name and arity so direct and two-hop aliases cannot escape.

World definition APIs borrow stable keys and clone only where semantic storage owns them. Scheduler completion carries raw JobCompletion and World; AppliedStep owns the output-key set; handlers derive reads, waits, changed facts, activation keys, and presentation data during dispatch. One activation-input event carries the whole completion. Tests select module identities through World rather than relying on HashSet order.

Program output is no longer telemetry. The runtime callback passes the existing rendered byte slice synchronously to an event-scoped OutputSink. Stdout writes immediately, retaining test sinks copy during the callback, and NullOutput does nothing. The fz.runtime.dbg event, handler, staging buffer, drains, and indirect-emitter exception are deleted.

Signal
Direct, recursive, unknown, computed-local, dead-store, branch, return, API-alias, helper-alias, UFCS, qualified direct, and qualified two-hop fixtures pin the guard. Raw pointer identity proves no output copy precedes the sink callback; retaining and null sink lifetimes are pinned; interpreter, JIT, CLI stdout, and AOT stdout parity pass. cargo test --lib passes 1,411 tests with 6 ignored and no failures. Runtime output tests pass 4/4. cargo fmt --all --check, workspace/all-target/all-feature check, strict workspace clippy, and cargo build --release --bin fz2 pass. The release fixture builds without diagnostics both with and without telemetry, both binaries exit zero, and JSON telemetry contains 1,055 events with no runtime.dbg event. No Rust comment block, lint allowance, shadow payload schema, telemetry-only counter, or retained staging buffer was added.

Final promotion audit discoveries
A borrowed helper formal was previously treated as raw authority solely because its type was &T. That admitted computed scalar and domain temporaries such as &items.len() and &make_world(), including aliases and two-hop helper chains. The guard now distinguishes primitive scalar channels from domain-authority channels, validates every known caller, follows borrowed aliases, accepts only proven existing places or references, and keeps mutable reborrows valid without accepting call expressions.

The interpreter destructor drain caught unpack_closure failures, emitted fz.runtime.bad_dtor_closure, and continued, converting a semantic runtime failure into optional telemetry and losing it when no handler was installed. The drain now returns the contextual closure-unpack error through its existing Result. The event and continuation path are deleted; valid destructor draining and program output behavior are unchanged.

Final promotion signal
All 12 guard fixtures and the production emitter audit pass. The computed-borrow fixture rejects direct, prebound, nested, aliased, and temporary-domain cases. Destructor propagation, four interpreter dtor cases, five destructor cases, and four runtime output tests pass. cargo test --lib passes 1,413 tests with 6 ignored and no failures. Formatting, workspace/all-target/all-feature check, strict workspace clippy, and release build pass. The release 00181 fixture builds without diagnostics with and without telemetry, both artifacts exit zero, and the 1,055-event JSONL trace contains neither runtime.dbg nor bad_dtor_closure.
title: Migrate raw-authority telemetry handlers and audit event payloads
